questionText:
Consider the following three ANSI-C programs, P1, P2, and P3.

P1P2P3
#include <stdio.h>

int a=5;
int main(){
  int a=7;
  return(0);
}		#include <stdio.h>

int main(){
  int a=5;
  int a=7;
  return(0);
}		#include <stdio.h>

int main(){
  int a=5;
  float a=7;
  return(0);
}

Which one of the following statements is true?
options: Only P1 will compile without any error
Only P2 will compile without any error
Only P3 will compile without any error
All three programs P1, P2, and P3 will compile without any error
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

1. Program P1: Declares a global variable a and a local variable a inside the main() function. The local variable shadows the global variable, which is completely valid C syntax. Hence, P1 compiles without any error.

2. Program P2: Attempts to declare the variable a twice within the same block scope (inside main()). Redefining a variable in the same scope causes a compile-time redeclaration error.

3. Program P3: Attempts to declare the variable a twice with conflicting data types (int and float) within the same block scope. This also causes a compile-time redeclaration error.

Therefore, only P1 will compile without any error, corresponding to Option (A).
